blocks.text: 4. Why This Matters Most for Production

blocks.content: Recall production mistakes being genuinely costly, already covered throughout the Security and Least Privilege topics, why this approval gate matters most, specifically here.
A dev environment mistake is genuinely cheap and quickly reversible, a production mistake genuinely is not, exactly the real distinction already established.
This is precisely why auto-apply for dev, and a real, deliberate approval gate for production, is the honest, practical, recommended default.

blocks.content: 6. A Real, Scoped List of Approvers
blocks.text: 6. A Real, Scoped List of Approvers

blocks.content: Recall Least Privilege, a real, scoped list of genuine, trusted approvers, not the entire team, should genuinely be configured for the production environment.
This directly applies the least-privilege principle already covered, this time specifically to who can genuinely approve a real, production change.
A real, small, deliberately-chosen group of trusted approvers keeps this genuine, real checkpoint meaningful, rather than a formality anyone can bypass.
This connects directly back to the real team member access section already covered in the Least Privilege topic's closing discussion.
This scoped list is worth reviewing periodically, exactly the same, real, recurring review discipline already covered throughout the Security module.
An approver who has genuinely changed roles, or left the team, should be removed from this real, live list promptly, not left indefinitely.

blocks.content: 7. A Real Approval Timeout
A real approval timeout avoids a genuinely stuck, live pipeline, waiting indefinitely for a real, human approval that may simply never actually come.
This small, real, practical detail keeps a genuine CI/CD system healthy, an abandoned, waiting pipeline job is worth automatically, genuinely expiring.
Configuring this deliberately, rather than leaving it unbounded, is a small, real, practical addition worth including in any real approval workflow.
This connects to the general, real operational awareness already covered throughout this module, a stuck pipeline is itself a real, worth-noticing problem.

blocks.alt: A real, deliberate timeout, avoiding a genuinely stuck, indefinitely-waiting, live pipeline

blocks.content: 8. A Real, Common Mistake
No real approval gate on production at all is a real, common mistake, especially for a team that started with only a dev environment and genuinely grew.
This often happens because the initial, real pipeline was built before production genuinely existed, and the gate was simply never, deliberately added.
The honest fix is exactly the pattern covered throughout this topic, added deliberately the moment a real, genuine production environment exists at all.
This mistake is worth checking for directly, in any real, existing pipeline, does production genuinely have its own, real approval gate configured.

9. Notifying Approvers
A real, waiting approval gate is only genuinely useful if a real, listed approver actually knows it is waiting, worth pairing with a real, direct notification.
Most real CI platforms support notifying a team chat channel, or a specific, real person, the moment an approval gate genuinely starts waiting.
Without this, a real, pending approval can genuinely sit unnoticed, quietly defeating the entire, real purpose of this checkpoint.
This connects directly back to the real, direct failure alerting already covered in the Apply Stage topic, applied here to a pending approval instead.
